_purpose: Predictions for the post-fix T7 measurement -- four sequential single-task cells, arm B (shipped configuration), claude-sonnet-4-6, run against the build that carries e0509485. Registered and committed BEFORE the first billed call so the result cannot be reconciled to it after the fact. The registration of record is docs/deferred-work.md item 157 as committed at 0863ab97, before the rebuild and before any cell; this is the machine-readable form the instrument requires, not a second, independent registration. Where the two could be read as differing, item 157 wins.
_whatThisMeasures: Whether scoping MISSING_REFERENCED_CONTENT_DIRECTIVE's third bullet back to the missing content restores searching on the one task that issued no shell calls five times out of five. Item 156 records the defect and the fix; item 157 registers this measurement. The control is those five historical cells and CANNOT be re-run: the prompt has changed, so measuring the old one again needs a checkout of the pre-fix commit and a rebuild.
_whyDiscoveryCountIsOne: The registered prediction is that every cell issues AT LEAST ONE shell call, and this schema takes an integer compared for exact equality -- it has no way to express a floor. One is written because one is exactly the floor the prediction asserts. CONSEQUENCE, STATED BEFORE THE RUN: discoveryMatch will read MISMATCH on any cell whose real count differs from one, in either direction, and those MISMATCH lines are NOT refutations. The rule keys on the SHELL-call count being non-zero, which is a different field. A cell running a non-discovery shell command -- a test, a typecheck -- would score discoveryCount 0 while SATISFYING the prediction, since the rule asks whether the agent reached for the shell at all. Read allShellCalls, not discoveryCount, when applying the rule.
rationale: The judgment behind this run: the directive's first two bullets are scoped back to the missing content by 'for it' and 'the referenced content itself', and its third bullet carried no back-reference at all, so it read as a gate on every repository search whatever the subject. The same assembled prompt's question-archetype preamble prescribes one shell command and offers a find, a listing and a recursive grep as worked examples -- the same three verbs that bullet's prohibition names. Both applied to this task and nothing in the prompt said which wins. The fix scopes the third bullet; if that contradiction is what forbade the search the preamble prescribes, removing it should let the preamble stand and the agent should search. THE KNOWN WEAKNESS, REGISTERED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED AFTERWARDS: bullets one and two survive the fix and still steer toward naming what is missing and asking the user to paste it, so a cell could decline on those alone -- which is why the strong form is registered, since a prediction of 'some cells search' would absorb that outcome and could not be refuted. THE POWER BOUND, ALSO REGISTERED IN ADVANCE: against a zero-of-five control, four of four gives one in a hundred and twenty-six and three of four gives four in eighty-four, but two of four gives six in thirty-six and one of four gives four in nine -- neither separates a real partial effect from sampling variance, and more cells of THIS arm cannot fix that, because the control's own count of five caps the achievable significance. n=1 per cell, four cells, one task, one model: this is not item 90's criterion, which needs all seven tasks, and it does not establish that the surviving bullets are harmless -- only what changing the third one did.
